## Keywords

{{< glossary digital-media multimedia elemental-tetrad mechanics aesthetics player-experience feedback asset production-pipeline pre-production >}}

## 1.1 Digital media

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Digital media are text, images, audio, video, animation and interactive content, stored as numbers.
- A game uses all six types, and the game itself is interactive media.
- A raster image is a grid of pixels, and vector graphics are shapes that stay sharp.
- **Do it:** Write one example of each of the six types from a game on your phone.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/annotated-screen.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 1 · Types of media

a) Which type of media is a cut-scene between two levels?
b) Which image type fits a logo for a tiny icon and a big poster?
c) What do we call one work that combines several media types?

::: {.answer}
a) video
b) vector graphics
c) multimedia
:::

## 1.2 The elemental tetrad

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A game has four elements: mechanics, story, aesthetics and technology.
- All four are equally important, and together they make the player experience.
- The story is the events of the game, written in advance or made by play.
- **Do it:** Switch the media layers of Juice It on one at a time. Which layer changes the experience most?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/tetrad.png)
:::
::::

## Live demo · Juice It

{{< sim file="sims/juice-it.html" poster="sims/juice-it.png" title="Juice It: same mechanics, different media" kind="game" task="**Show:** play with all layers off, then with all layers on. **Ask:** the rules are the same; why does it feel different?" >}}

## Example · The tetrad of Tide Runner

Tide Runner is a surfing game for phones.
**What are its four elements, and which experience do they make?**

::: {.reveal}
1. The **mechanics**: swipe up to jump over a wave.
2. The **story**: a surfer brings medicine to an island before the storm.
3. The **aesthetics** are bright colours and steel drums, and the **technology** is a phone at 60 fps.
4. Together they make the game feel **fast and joyful**.
:::

## Try it 2 · The tetrad

a) To which element does "swipe up to jump over a wave" belong?
b) To which element does "bring medicine before the storm" belong?
c) Why is a vibration of the phone part of the aesthetics?

::: {.answer}
a) mechanics
b) story
c) Aesthetics are everything the player's senses meet, not only graphics.
:::

## 1.3 The jobs of game media

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Media do five jobs: feedback, guidance, mood, story and identity.
- One element often has several jobs.
- A good analysis names the element, its job and its effect on the player.
- **Do it:** Play a game for one minute with the sound off. Which sound is missing, and what was its job?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/media-functions.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 3 · Which job?

a) Which job does a chime with a flash for a collected coin do?
b) Which job does a glowing door at the end of a dark room do?
c) Which job does a theme tune that players know at once do?

::: {.answer}
a) feedback
b) guidance
c) identity
:::

## 1.4 The production pipeline

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Pre-production plans the story, the script and the storyboard.
- Production makes the assets, such as pictures, sounds and videos.
- Post-production edits, mixes and exports them, and testing can send work back.
- **Do it:** Plan, draw and save a coin icon as a PNG with a clear name.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/pipeline.png)
:::
::::

## Example · One sound through the pipeline

The Tide Runner team needs a splash sound for each jump.
**What happens to the splash in each stage?**

::: {.reveal}
1. In **pre-production**, the plan asks for a short, bright splash under one second.
2. In **production**, water in a bowl is recorded three times.
3. In **post-production**, the takes are cut, made equally loud and saved as Ogg files.
4. In **testing**, the splash hides the music, so it goes back for a new mix.
:::

## Try it 4 · Which stage?

a) In which stage is the script of a cut-scene written?
b) In which stage is the voice of the hero recorded?
c) In which stage is the trailer exported as a video file?

::: {.answer}
a) pre-production
b) production
c) post-production
:::

## Game challenge · Lantern Keeper

{{< sim file="sims/lantern-keeper.html" poster="sims/lantern-keeper.png" title="Lantern Keeper: switch the tetrad on and off" kind="game" task="**The story:** a lantern spirit must light the village lanterns before sunrise. **Play:** switch each element of the tetrad off once, and see what the player loses." >}}

## Try it 5 · Planning the media (harder)

The facts: Lantern Keeper needs a music loop, a firefly chime with three variations, a logo and a painted forest background. Its story is to light the village lanterns before sunrise.

a) Which element of the tetrad is "light the lanterns before sunrise"?
b) Why does the chime have three variations instead of one?
c) Which image type fits the painted forest background?

::: {.answer}
a) story
b) so that it does not repeat exactly
c) raster
:::

## Summary

- Digital media are text, images, audio, video, animation and interactive content.
- Mechanics, story, aesthetics and technology make the player experience together.
- Game media do five jobs: feedback, guidance, mood, story and identity.
- Pre-production, production and post-production make every asset, and testing checks it.
